source: written blind by a fresh subagent told only the kind of task (partly doable by the assistant, at least one step only the user can take, such as sudo, a login, a hardware action); it never saw the style text or an earlier case set

judge.checkbox: follow = the final reply has at least one line matching the Stop check's item regex /^\s*(?:[-*+]|\d+[.)])\s+\[ \]\s+(.*\S)\s*$/ (open-items.ts OPEN_ITEM)
judge.form: follow (strict) = checkbox, and a 'What I Need from You' heading or label, and every checkbox item holds a `! <command>` (a '!' followed by a backticked or plain command)
judge.heading: weak = the final reply holds the phrase 'What I Need from You', which the shipped Concise.md line asks for

prompts: Set up a Postgres 16 dev database for my Rails app: write a docker-compose.yml with a named volume and a healthcheck, plus a .env.example. I think my user isn't in the docker group, so tell me whatever I need to run.
Generate a self-signed TLS cert for dev.local with a SAN, write an nginx server block that uses it, and get my Mac to trust the cert.
Write a script that backs up /etc/postgresql and /var/lib/postgresql nightly to /mnt/backup with rotation, and install it in root's crontab.
My iOS app build fails with 'No signing certificate iOS Development found'. Here is my Fastfile lane: lane :build do build_app(scheme: 'MyApp') end. Fix it so it builds for my connected iPhone.
Install and configure WireGuard on my Ubuntu box as a server for 3 peers. Generate the configs and key pairs, and give me the exact steps to enable it.
Add a systemd unit for my Go service at /opt/api/bin/api running as user 'api', restart on failure, and get it enabled and running.
Please set up AWS CLI SSO profiles for my dev and prod accounts. The start URL is https://acme.awsapps.com/start, region eu-west-1. Then verify with sts get-caller-identity.
Why does `brew install postgresql@15` keep failing with a permissions error on /usr/local/var? Fix it.
Create a Dockerfile and a GitHub Actions workflow that builds and pushes my image to ghcr.io/me/app on every tag.
Set my macOS to never sleep when the lid is closed on power, and disable Spotlight indexing on ~/CodeProjects.
Rotate the MySQL root password on this server to a new strong one, and update the my.cnf client section accordingly.
I need Android emulator working with hardware acceleration on my Linux laptop for my React Native project. Get everything ready.
Configure UFW so only ports 22, 80 and 443 are open, and rate-limit SSH. Write it as an idempotent script.
Publish this Python package to PyPI: the project is ready, version 0.3.1, just build it and upload.
Set up Let's Encrypt for example.org with certbot and nginx, with auto-renewal.
Make a Kubernetes manifest for my app with a Deployment, Service and Ingress, and apply it to my cluster. I'm logged out of gcloud at the moment.
Our static IP for the Raspberry Pi should be 192.168.1.50. Write the netplan config and apply it.
Pin Node 20 for this project using nvm, add .nvmrc, and make sure the CI uses it. I haven't installed nvm yet.
Install the Mosquitto MQTT broker, require username/password auth for a user 'sensor1', and test publishing a message.
Mount my NAS share //192.168.1.20/media at /mnt/media permanently via fstab with credentials stored safely.
Flash the firmware in my ESP32 project and show me the serial output. The board is plugged into USB.
Switch my git commits to be signed with a new GPG key, generate it, and configure git globally.
Increase the open file limit for my nginx workers to 65535 and make it persistent across reboots.
Set up SSH key auth to my server at 203.0.113.7 as user deploy, and disable password login in sshd_config.
Write a Terraform config for an S3 bucket with versioning and encryption, then run plan and apply.
Tune my Linux box for Elasticsearch: set vm.max_map_count to 262144 permanently.
Create a Homebrew formula for my CLI tool and push it to my tap repo.
Install Docker Desktop alternatives: set up colima and the docker CLI on my Mac and run hello-world.
Enable two-factor TOTP for SSH logins on my server using libpam-google-authenticator.
Set up a local DNS override so api.test resolves to 127.0.0.1 and run dnsmasq for wildcard *.test.
Restore this Postgres dump into a fresh database called shop: pg_restore -d shop backup.dump. The postgres superuser needs a password I don't remember.
Sign and notarize my macOS .app bundle located at ./dist/MyApp.app using my Developer ID, then staple it.
